subtopic: Operator-level IR vs. Loop / Tensor-expression IR
learningObjective: Distinguish the abstractions and capabilities of graph-/operator-level IR (e.g., XLA HLO, ONNX) from loop/tensor-expression-level IR (e.g., TVM TensorIR, MLIR linalg/affine).
stem: Which of the following statements correctly distinguish operator-level IR (e.g., XLA HLO, ONNX) from loop-/tensor-expression-level IR (e.g., TVM TensorIR, MLIR linalg or affine)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Loop-level IRs are strictly required to make graph-level fusion decisions such as which pairs of ops to fuse, because operator-level IRs cannot express fusion of any kind and depend on lowering to loop dialects first.
Loop-level IRs support tiling, unrolling, and vectorization at the IR level, whereas operator-level IRs delegate such transformations to a lower-level compiler or kernel library.
Operator-level IRs can carry static tensor shape and dtype annotations on SSA-like values without exposing loop structure, enabling shape-based rewrites at the graph level.
Operator-level IRs represent computations as coarse-grained ops (matmul, softmax, layernorm) with implicit iteration; loop-level IRs make loops, iteration variables, and memory indexing explicit.

explanation: A: Operator-level IRs use op abstractions with implicit loops (matmul, conv); loop-level IRs make iteration explicit (for-loops, index expressions). B is false: HLO and TVM Relax both perform graph/operator-level fusion (producer-consumer, epilogue) without exposing loops; fusion is not restricted to loop IRs. C: Tile/unroll/vectorize are canonically loop-IR transformations (affine, linalg tiling passes, TensorIR schedules). D: HLO and ONNX carry per-value shape/dtype annotations natively.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: operator-level fusion is a well-established capability (XLA HLO fusion, TensorFlow's grappler, TVM Relax operator fusion).
optionExplanations.B: Correct: loop-level transformations (tile, unroll, vectorize, parallelize) require explicit iteration to name.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: HLO and ONNX both use static shape/dtype annotations on SSA-like values.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: this is the canonical distinction between the two levels.

assumptions: The comparison is between typical instances of each IR level (HLO for operator-level; TensorIR / MLIR linalg for loop-level), acknowledging that some frameworks bridge both.
nonImplications: Does not imply that operator-level and loop-level IRs cannot coexist in the same compiler; MLIR's dialect layering explicitly supports both.
Does not imply that loop-level IR is 'better'; it is more expressive for transformations but less compact for coarse-grained op patterns.

distractorRationales.A: Confuses fusion with loop-level transformations; graph-level fusion is real.
